title: How do we write four thirds as a whole and a fraction?
description: Four thirds is written the way the book writes three halves, as a whole number plus a fraction. The board adds four thirds, takes three thirds as one whole and keeps the third that is left. Keeko doubts the size of the leftover piece.
teaching_notes: One idea: the leftover piece keeps the same size as the parts, so the bottom number does not change. Watch for students who write the leftover with the top number as its bottom number.

source: We saw that 3/2 = 1 + 1/2. Write 4/3 in a similar way.
video_script.why: A learner writes a fraction greater than one as a whole number plus a fraction by taking out the whole.
video_script.substitution: the book's own fraction four thirds, written like three halves
video_script.anchor: four third-unit bars on a number line from 0 to 2
video_script.wrong_answer: four thirds is one plus one fourth, because the top number is four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko names the leftover piece with the top number, though the leftover is still a third.
video_script.payoff_line: Four thirds is one plus one third

final_answer.spoken: four thirds is one plus one third

video_script.fraction_reading: one third, three thirds, four thirds, one fourth
maths_rules: 1 third is left over, and it is still 1/3
video_script.design: Four third bars laid from zero. Three join into one whole bar and the fourth stays as a third.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the line 3/2 = 1 + 1/2 written; below it 4/3 = ?

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.known: the line three halves equals one plus one half is written
marks.ask: under it, four thirds equals a blank box

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a line you have seen.
<bookmark mark='known'/>We saw that three halves is one plus one half.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write four thirds in a similar way?

beats.on_screen: the two lines stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: four third bars in a row from 0; a whole unit bar beside them as long as three third bars

marks.bars: four third bars of equal size line up from zero
marks.whole: a whole unit bar is shown beside them, as long as three third bars

narration: <bookmark mark='bars'/>Four thirds means four parts, and each part is one third of a unit.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>A whole unit is the same length as three of those thirds.

beats.on_screen: Given: the fraction 4/3, and 3/2 = 1 + 1/2 as the model
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fraction is four thirds, and the model is three halves.

beats.on_screen: To find: 4/3 as a whole number plus a fraction
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write four thirds as a whole number plus a fraction.

marks.split: four thirds is written as four thirds added together

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, write four thirds as four thirds added together. That is one third four times.

marks.whole: the first three third bars join into one whole unit bar

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step two, the first three thirds make one whole. Three times one third is one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: one third is left, and it is still 1/3

marks.left: the fourth third bar stays alone and keeps its label one third

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, one third is left over. It is the same size as before, so it is still one third.

beats.on_screen: Check: 3/3 + 1/3 = 4/3, the same as the start

marks.check: the whole unit and the left over third are put back together as four thirds

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, put the pieces back together. Three thirds and one third make four thirds again.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Four thirds is one plus one third.
It is one whole unit and one third more.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the third bars
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 4/3 is 1 plus 1/4 because the top number is 4; the leftover bar is put against a third bar and they match; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.match: the leftover bar is placed against a third bar and they match exactly
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the leftover is labelled one third

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four thirds is one plus one fourth, because the top number is four.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Put the leftover piece against a third. It matches exactly, so it is one third.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The pieces stay thirds, so the bottom number stays three.
